slides.text: I work in accounts payable at Central Interior Appliances—domain name cia-corp.org. For the past six months, a four-star general has been accidentally copying me on classified black-ops briefings. At first, I tried emailing back to explain that I approve dishwasher rebates in Ohio, not regime changes in the Balkans. They thought I was speaking in deep-cover cipher and promoted my clearance level.

Last Tuesday, an operative named Viper submitted an urgent requisition for 'Operation Nightfall: three unmarked helicopters and forty bricks of C4.' I had to step in. 'Per company policy,' I replied-all to the Joint Chiefs, 'any expense over $500 requires three competing vendor quotes and a signed W-9. Also, Viper still hasn't uploaded his Chili's receipt from Prague. Denied.'

Thirty seconds later, the Director of National Intelligence replied: 'Apologies, sir. Viper has been reprimanded and is scanning the Chili's receipt now. Will two helicopters in economy class suffice?' I approved it with a stern warning about Q3 budget bloat. Honestly, global espionage is running forty percent under budget this quarter, and the Pentagon just sent me a branded fleece vest.
